messages:
Samir Chen: Quick heads-up — ran a focused comparison between kernel-A and kernel-B for the rerank/embedding endpoint using both synthetic traffic and the replay harness. Seeing a consistent tail latency bump (~95th-99th) when kernel selector flips to kernel-B at batch sizes > 48 with cold KV cache.

Priya Rao: Can you paste the exact harness command you ran? and which model size/dims?

Samir Chen: replay-harness run --source=s3://replays/2026-03/queries --concurrency=200 --batching=dynamic --kernel-threshold=48 --kv-policy=auto --model=rw-embed-1024. Used 1024-dim vectors; payloads ~1.2KB per item (metadata+vec).

Diego Marquez: perf-bot attached profiling dump (flame) shows an increased memcpy/alloc time when kernel-B is selected. Looks like kernel-B forces a slightly different memory layout -> extra copies for batched KV lookups.

perf-bot: Profiling summary: p95 latency kernel-A=38ms, kernel-B=54ms; p99 kernel-A=68ms, kernel-B=114ms. 30% more CPU sys time, 1.8x allocations when kernel-B active.

Natalie Li: Interesting — does this reproduce on synthetic traffic (no replay) or only replay with realistic key locality?

Samir Chen: I ran synthetic uniform traffic (same rps/concurrency) and the regressed tail is much smaller: kernel-A p99=72ms, kernel-B p99=85ms. So replay/locality + cold KV cache amplify the effect.

Priya Rao: That suggests KV cache behavior is interacting with batching heuristics + kernel selection. If kernel-B expects contiguous KV pages and current KV store returns fragmented segments, we pay for consolidation.

Diego Marquez: Agreed. Two follow-ups: 1) We should add a micro-benchmark that simulates KV miss/repopulate with same object sizes. 2) Record kernel selection decisions per request in traces (we have traces but not per-request kernel tag).

Samir Chen: I pushed a small change to the replay harness to emit `kernel_choice` as a tag in traces and instrumented KV hit-rate per batch. Patch: `git rev: fb3a1d2` — running longer replay now (30m) to collect stables.

Priya Rao: Also try forcing kernel-A for a run with identical replay to get apples-to-apples: same preheat sequence, same seed. We need matching warmup profiles because KV state is huge.

perf-bot: Smoke runs queued: (1) replay forcing kernel-A, (2) replay forcing kernel-B, (3) synthetic with fragmented-KV emulation.

Natalie Li: If kernel-A always wins on tail for embedding dims >=1024 with payloads >1KB, we should consider raising the selection threshold or adding a cost model that includes KV fragmentation cost. But need numbers across dims 512/768/1024 and payload sizes 0.5KB/1KB/2KB.

Samir Chen: Agreed. My plan: run matrix (dims x payload x kernel) with both synthetic fragmented KV and replay. Each run ~15m, will collect p50/p95/p99, allocs, memcpy time. Will share results in the next thread.

Priya Rao: Thanks — also add a check for batching window sizes: dynamic batching sometimes groups heterogenous sequence lengths which may change kernel heuristics. Maybe try fixed batching at 32/64 too.

Diego Marquez: FYI I reproduced the memcpy hotspot locally with a small harness that replicates batch assembly. I'll open a tiny PR to avoid double-copy when building the batched KV request.

Samir Chen: Perfect. If Diego's PR reduces allocs, we can re-run kernel-B and see if tail improves. If not, we consider moving kernel selection earlier (pre-batch) or a runtime fallback to kernel-A for batches with >X fragmented KV hits.

Natalie Li: Tagging @oncall for perf regression tracking. We should put an alert if p99 > 100ms for rerank endpoint in prod canary.

Priya Rao: One more note — when comparing synthetic vs replay, we must align the encryption/compression flags on KV (those change payload size and memory copy patterns). Document this in the benchmark README so apples-to-apples is maintained.

Samir Chen: Will do. Thanks everyone — I'll drop the matrix CSV and flame graphs when runs finish. :coffee:

Diego Marquez: :thumbsup: and I'll link the PR when ready.
